These petitions coming on for admission this day, the co

 Order
1] Heard finally, with the consent of the parties.

2] This order shall govern the disposal of M.Cr.C.
Nos.27431 of 2023 and 22993 of 2020, as in the aforesaid petitions, the same FIR is sought to be quashed.

3] This petition has been filed by the petitioner, Abdul Salam under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the FIR lodged at Crime No.172/2020 at Police Station Nalkheda, District- Agar Malwa,
under Sections 467, 421, 420, 406, 201 and 120-B of the IPC as also the subsequent proceedings arising out the aforesaid crime number.

4] In brief, the facts of the case are that the FIR in the present case was lodged on 20.06.2020 in respect of a transaction which took place between the complainant Abdul Rajik and the accused Mohammad Juber.

It was alleged in the FIR that Mohammad Juber had entered into an agreement with the complainant Abdul Rajik on 19.03.2019 for sale of land situated at Survey No.207/1, 207/2 and 207/3 of different measurements, for a total consideration of Rs.4,51,00,000/-, which according to the complainant, was given to the accused Mohammad Juber in cash.

However, despite receiving the aforesaid amount, the accused has refused to execute the sale deed and in this regard, in the Panchayat of the village also, he has given additional amount of Rs.44,00,000/- to Mohammad Juber and thus, in all the total sum of Rs.4,95,00,000/- have already been received by the accused Mohammad Juber, who has refused to Abdul Salam vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184323305/

It was also stated in the FIR that initially,
the accused Mohammad Juber had entered into an agreement with five persons on 19.03.2019 and,
on the basis of the said agreement, the land was also transferred in his name through a registered sale deed dated 08.08.2019.

5] Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the present petitioner Abdul Salam's name does not find place in the FIR and only during the course of investigation, a memo under Section 27 of the Evidence Act has been obtained from him, in which he has stated that the original agreement which took place between the complainant Abdul Rajik and accused Mohammad Juber has already been torn and thrown away by him.
It is also submitted that subsequently, the aforesaid agreement has already been recovered at the instance of Mohammad Juber on 21.09.2020.
Counsel has submitted that apart from the aforesaid memo, there is nothing to connect the petitioner with the offence.
Thus, it is submitted that no case for continuation of proceedings is made out and thus, the FIR and the subsequent proceedings be quashed.

6] Counsel appearing for the objector Abdul Rajik has vehemently opposed the prayer and it is submitted that the present petitioner Abdul Salam was hand in gloves with the main accused Mohammad Juber as the same land which the complainant was to purchase for a consideration of Rs.4,95,00,000/- has been sold by the accused Mohammad Juber to Abdul Salam for a consideration of Rs.2,50,00,000/- vide sale deed dated 08.06.2020, which has already been proved in evidence at the instance of PW-1 Abdul Rajik.
It is also submitted that only the I.O. remains to the examined in the Trial Court, as five material witnesses have already been examined in the Trial Court.
7] Counsel for the State has also opposed the prayer and it is submitted that no case for interference is made out.
8] Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.

9] On perusal of the record, it is found that although a memo under Section 27 of the Evidence Act has been prepared at the instance of the present petitioner Abdul Salam, however, it is also a matter of record that a part of the land was also sold by Mohd. Juber to the present petitioner Abdul Salam.
10] In such circumstances, at this stage, it is difficult to form an opinion that the petitioner was not hand in gloves with the main accused Mohd. Juber, and was not at all involved in the case.

Since the material witnesses have already been examined, the appreciation of their testimony recorded in the Trial Court would fall within the realm of the Trial Court only, thus, in such circumstances, this Court does not find it to be a fit case to interfere.
Accordingly, the petition being devoid of merits, is hereby dismissed.
11] It is also made clear that this Court has not reflected upon the merits of the case and the Trial Court shall be solely guided by the evidence which has been adduced by the parties on record.

12] So far as M.Cr.C. No.22993/2020 is concerned, it has been filed by the main accused Mohammad Juber, under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the FIR lodged at Crime No.172/2020 at Police Station Nalkheda, District- Agar Malwa, under Sections 467, 421, 420, 406, 201 and 120-B of the IPC as also the subsequent proceedings arising out the aforesaid crime number.

sentences.text: Counsel appearing for the petitioner has submitted that the entire transaction of Rs.4,95,00,000/- is a cash transaction as admitted by the complainant.
However, there is not an iota of evidence available in the charge-sheet to demonstrate that any amount was ever paid to the petitioner.

It is further submitted that earlier this Court had also granted anticipatory bail to the petitioner taking note of the fact that the entire transaction is a cash transaction and the payment of which, has also not been proved.
14] Counsel has also submitted that the petitioner had entered into an agreement with the original land holders, which was subsequently sold to him through a registered sale deed.

Counsel has further submitted that the complainant has already filed a civil suit for specific performance of the contract and thus, when the lis is pending in the Civil Court, there was no occasion for the Police to lodge the FIR.
15] Counsel appearing for the objector has submitted that civil and criminal remedies are two different remedies and there is no straight jacket formula that if the civil suit is filed, in that case,
criminal case cannot proceed.
Thus, it is submitted that as five witnesses have already been examined and only the I.O. remains to be examined as the last witness, no case for interference, at this stage, is made out.
16] Counsel for the State has also opposed the prayer and it is submitted that looking to the criminal antecedents of the petitioner, no case for interference is made out.
17] Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.

18] On perusal of the record, considering the fact that huge monetary transactions have taken place, and the prima facie involvement of the present petitioner cannot be ruled out, hence, merely because a civil suit has also been filed by the complainant, it cannot be said that it is a case of civil nature only, as this Court is of the considered opinion that a remedy of Civil Court can also be resorted to by the complainant only with a view to ensure that he should not miss out on any legal remedy.

19] It is also found that the material witnesses have already been examined and as has been informed by the counsel for the respondent, only the I.O. remains to be examined in the Trial Court as a last witness, thus, when the trial itself is at its fag end, this Court is of the considered opinion that it is not a fit case to exercise jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. to quash the FIR at this stage.
20] Accordingly, the petition stands dismissed.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Bahar Abdul Salam vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184323305/
